verdict.reasoning: Patient reports cough and constantly streaming nose starting about 5 days ago: "five days ago I started having problems like a cough, and my nose is just constantly streaming" and later confirms "five days or so ago"; cough described as "quite dry".

Cough frequency and character: "I'm coughing maybe every twenty, thirty minutes or so"; dry with no sputum: "It's kind of quite dry" and "you bringing up any phlegm at all? Patient: No." No hemoptysis: "Have you coughed up any blood or anything like that? Patient: Nope."

No chest pain, SOB, or pleuritic pain: "Any chest pain?... Patient: Uh, no" and "Any difficulty breathing, feeling short of breath or any pain when you take a deep breath? Patient: No, that's all fine."
Green rhinorrhea and no epistaxis: patient notes constant streaming nose and when asked about blood, says "And any blood coming from the nose? Patient: No, it's pretty green."

Subjective fevers/chills without measurement: "I've been feeling really hot... sometimes I'm feeling really chilly" and when asked, "Have you checked your temperature with a thermometer? Patient: Uhh, no, I haven't."
Myalgias reported and no headache/visual changes: "Any headaches or change in your vision? Patient: No, um, I've had quite achy muscles, but that's pretty much it."

Brief diarrhea at onset now resolved: "around when it started, I had some diarrhoea, but I don't know if that was associated. But since then it's all been pretty fine." and later confirms "No vomiting, diarrhoea now? Patient: No."
Eating and drinking okay: "And are you eating and drinking normally? Patient: Uhh, yes." and "you're drinking well, holding down fluids OK? Patient: Yeah."
History of diabetes and hypertension: patient says "I'm diabetic" and later "I've got hypertension... but that's it, really." and confirms "just the hypertension and the diabetes."

Metformin and lisinopril: "I think something called metformin, and lisinopril I think is the other one." Lemsip 2–3 times/day: "a quite a few lemon sips... maybe two or three. Maybe, like, at the start of the day and at the end of the day." (Lemsip is a brand cold remedy).
Mild hay fever and no drug allergies: "I sometimes suffer from some, like, hay fever. But, um, but it's not bad" and "Any allergies to any medications at all? Patient: Not that I'm aware of, no."
Living situation and job: "Who do you live with at home? Patient: Uh, my partner and my dog." and "Do you work? Patient: Uh, yes. I'm an office manager."
Occasional alcohol: "You drink any alcohol? Patient: Yes, the odd cherry." (interpreted as occasional drink).

Recent normal diabetes labs and no SMBG: "with your diabetes, have you had a blood test recently? Patient: ... Yeah, it was normal. It was around three weeks ago." and later "Do you have blood sugar checking equipment? Do you check? No, OK."

Acute cough and coryza 5 days: history confirms 5 days of cough and nasal streaming. Doctor impression: "it sounds like you, you probably have got an infection in the chest... these infections are caused by viruses" and describes self-limiting course with no red-flag findings (no SOB, chest pain, hemoptysis, etc.). Viral URTI vs viral bronchitis is a reasonable direct clinical inference.

DM on metformin: "something called metformin". No hyperglycemic symptoms: denies polyuria and polydipsia: "Any increase in frequency... or any increased thirst? Patient: Uh, no, not particularly." Recent labs normal: "Yeah, it was normal. It was around three weeks ago." No SMBG: "Do you have blood sugar checking equipment? Do you check? No, OK."

Hypertension on lisinopril: "lisinopril I think is the other one." BP control unknown: "when did you last have your blood pressure checked? Patient: Uh, ooh, uh, a while ago" and "Do you know if it's been stable? Patient: Uh, I can't remember."

Continue Lemsip and avoid other paracetamol: "It's fine to carry on what you're doing at the moment, with the lemsip. I wouldn't take, and that, that contains paracetamol so don't take any other paracetamol containing products, um, with that at the same time."

Avoid daytime cough syrup, small amount at night: "the cough syrup isn't advisable in the daytime because it's best for your body if you just keep coughing. But if you're kept up all night and you can't sleep at all, then it, it's OK to have a little bit of cough syrup, just to settle that down."
Advice to get thermometer and monitor temperature: "it's definitely worth getting a thermometer and checking your temperature." and "The important thing to do would be to take your temperature."

Safety-net advice: "if the temperature's ongoing... or your cough's getting worse, you're coughing up lots of nasty phlegm or you cough up any blood or get blood coming out your nose, um, or any shortness of breath, chest pain, then we certainly would need to speak to you again."

Expected course: "most of the time, these infections are caused by viruses, so they do normally settle by themselves. But it can take, you know, a week or two, um, and you can persistently have the cough ongoing longer than that."
Maintain regular DM follow-up: "Well, if you make sure that you have the regular diabetes and blood pressure checkups that your GP has asked you for?"

BP follow-up and lisinopril dose review are implied: doctor asks when BP was last checked and if stable, then advises "make sure that you have the regular... blood pressure checkups that your GP has asked you for," which entails arranging BP checks and thereby reviewing management including lisinopril dose. This is a direct clinical inference from the plan.
